sources.title: Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation: Our History
sources.note: Direct tribal history; political economy, postwar Cassacinamon communities, 1983 settlement and economic initiatives. No aggregate death toll or claim every warrior was absent from Mistick adopted.

sources.title: Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation: Welcome and tribal identity
sources.note: Direct homepage, exact Wuyeepuyôq / Welcome; present institutional writing. Current revenue totals omitted.

sources.title: Mashantucket Pequot Museum battlefield project: The Pequot War
sources.note: Direct project history, 1637 Mistick campaign and 1638 Hartford treaty. No exact casualty count used.

sources.title: Mashantucket Pequot Museum: 1700s Pequot Farmstead Guide, 2023
sources.note: Direct two-page museum guide: reconstructed farmstead context, markers 1/2/4/8/12/18. Later introduced fruit trees are not projected into precontact period.

sources.title: Connecticut Department of Education: History of the Eastern Pequot Tribal Nation
sources.note: Direct state teaching page presenting Eastern Pequot history, 1670s settlement and 1683 formal deed; living community distinct from Mashantucket.

sources.title: Eastern Pequot Tribal Nation: Archaeology
sources.note: Direct/indexed official community account, partnership since 2003, ten housing sites and pottery/household objects, 2019 transfer of collection. Not an excavation report supporting precise house dates.

sources.title: Eastern Pequot Tribal Nation: Reservation and infrastructure
sources.note: Direct/indexed official homepage: 2021 state funding approved for septic system, well, roads and tribal-office infrastructure. Approval not described as completion.

sources.title: Mashantucket Pequot Museum: Thirteen Moons
sources.note: Direct/indexed community presentation, contemporary Green Corn/Schemitzun celebration and winter storytelling. Unrelated multi-nation artist biographies not treated as universal Pequot customs.

sources.title: Mohegan Tribe: Educational history and cultural overview
sources.note: Direct 42-page tribal educational document hosted by Connecticut. Printed pp.3-4 oral learning; pp.8-10 Uncas, land divisions and later work. Migration traditions not treated as archaeologically exact chronology.

sources.title: Margaret Bruchac: Of Shells and Ship’s Nails
sources.note: Direct researcher’s first-person collections examination, 2014 with 2017 update. Fort Shantok nail10289, bead10221, shell blanks, polishing stones. Drill-bit interpretation attributed; no speculative Viking chronology or definite ship origin adopted.

sources.title: Mohegan Tribe: Tantaquidgeon Museum artifacts
sources.note: Direct tribal collection description: circa1638 Uncas collar, clam/conch shell, community interpretation of white triangles. No universal uniqueness claim repeated.

sources.title: The Huntington: Object Story, Basket
sources.note: Direct collection record, J.H.S. (Mohegan), circa1880, ash splint and dye, 2016.25.50. Distinguishes this named-culture object from another regionally attributed basket on same page.

sources.title: Mohegan Tribe: Wigwam Festival
sources.note: Direct/indexed tribal account, 1860 Emma Baker revival, later church fundraising, yokeag and contemporary ice cream serving. No fixed1492 calendar claimed.

sources.title: Mohegan Tribe: Samson Occom
sources.note: Direct/indexed community biography, fund-raising disappointment, move to Oneida lands and April2022 agreement to return papers. Does not adopt first-ordained-minister superlative.

sources.title: Mohegan Tribe: Fidelia Fielding
sources.note: Direct/indexed tribe account, language spoken with Martha Uncas, diary preservation and 2020 return agreement. Avoids calling language or community extinct.

sources.title: Fidelia Fielding: Diary transcription and gloss, entry of 30 May 1904
sources.note: Direct PDF hosted by Brothertown Indian Nation, page1. First line is Stephanie Fielding’s transcription of original spelling, second Speck phonetic, third English gloss, fourth modern respelling. Sample uses original-spelling line, not modern reconstruction. Old Cornell custody header superseded by2020 agreement.

sources.title: Mohegan Tribe: Gladys Tantaquidgeon
sources.note: Direct tribal biography, herbal learning and comparative research, museum1931, records supporting1994recognition. Research among other nations distinguished from Mohegan practice.

sources.title: Connecticut DEEP: Tribal Affairs
sources.note: Direct/indexed state relationship inventory, Mohegan1994federal acknowledgment and continuing government. No current membership totals.

sources.title: Mohegan Tribe: IMLS 2020 library and garden project proposal
sources.note: Indexed original grant proposal describes existing library story times, book clubs, workshops and museum gardens. Proposed project outcomes not claimed completed.

sources.title: Mashantucket Pequot Museum: Pequot War and Hartford treaty
sources.note: Same URL as Pequot card; combined URL budget counted across both narratives. Mohegan alliance and1638 treaty role only.

geometry.assessment: Restricted southeastern Connecticut coastal outline, not either modern reservation; broader historical homeland extends beyond this small outline.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Generic Pequot narrative with separate Mashantucket and Eastern Pequot community history, no alias absorption and no common modern governmental status inferred.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Postwar communities, eighteenth-century reconstructed farmstead and modern infrastructure explicitly later than map interval. Treaty defeat separated from continuing people.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Direct contemporary Mashantucket government Wuyeepuyôq / Welcome, no precontact alphabet implied.

geometry.assessment: Broad southeastern Connecticut ancestral-region outline, not modern reservation geometry or a reliable1492 boundary for Uncas’s later polity.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Separate Mohegan narrative; related Pequot language and ancestry do not justify merging political identities. No Mahican/Mohican identity confusion.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Opening explicitly states seventeenth-century political differentiation postdates imported1492 record. Nineteenth-century festival and1904 diary are later evidence.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Fielding May30 1904 diary, original-spelling line transcribed by Stephanie Fielding, Speck English gloss. No modern reconstructed line substituted for historic spelling.
